output.summary: KEP-3257 introduces a cluster-scoped ClusterTrustBundle object in certificates.k8s.io so in-cluster signers can publish X.509 trust anchors, plus a kubelet clusterTrustBundle projected volume source to deliver them to workloads. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Kubernetes had no standard way for signers to distribute trust anchors; the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap required over-broad permissions to create ConfigMaps in all namespaces, and static anchors embedded in webhook/aggregated API configs complicate rotation. A dedicated cluster-scoped type allows separate RBAC (wide read, locked-down write) and a projected volume gives workloads filesystem access. The status is implemented, so the design was carried through.

alternatives.option: Use ConfigMaps for trust bundles (status quo kube-root-ca.crt pattern)
alternatives.why_not: Creating a ConfigMap in every namespace requires granting over-broad permissions to the responsible controller (create ConfigMaps in all namespaces).

alternatives.option: Keep static trust anchor sets embedded in webhook/aggregated API configuration
alternatives.why_not: Static trust anchor sets embedded directly in configuration complicate the job of rotating the backing CA's roots of trust.

alternatives.option: Use a cluster-scoped CRD per signer, as one signer implementation does
alternatives.why_not: CRDs work well, but are inappropriate for use by core APIs.

alternatives.option: Federation via multiple trust anchor sets within one object
alternatives.why_not: The author dropped the federation piece, converting ClusterTrustBundle to a single set of trust anchors, and said federation can be handled with a note or version field in spec.

evidence.quote: Each of these approaches has downsides: * Creating a ConfigMap in every namespace requires granting over-broad permissions to the responsible controller
This KEP introduces the certificates.k8s.io ClusterTrustBundle cluster-scoped object, a vehicle for in-cluster certificate signers to communicate their trust anchors to workloads.
ClusterTrustBundles have an optional `spec.signerName` field that associates them to a signer. Admission control is used to prevent spoofing.
I'm going to drop the federation piece --- convert ClusterTrustBundle to just be a single set of trust anchors.
We decided to not read them in the kube-apiserver for alpha. reassess at beta.
